goal: must rebuild Flow command authority boundaries on the current main baseline so Flow artifacts are governed by base-side artifact authority, implementation and Git operations are governed by execution checkout authority, and both worktree and non-worktree Flow use the same explicit authority model.

analysis.problem: Current Flow code still exposes authority-sensitive operations through raw repository or root strings in enough places that artifact paths, execution checkout paths, fingerprint inputs, and recovery evidence can be mixed across command boundaries. Issue #494 frames this as new work on current main because the older #491 branch diverged from target identity and recovery changes from #489-#493.
analysis.proposedApproach: Introduce or complete explicit authority objects around FlowWorkspace for artifact storage, execution checkout, and command-level coordination; migrate Flow artifact reads and writes, Git/test execution, file-map reconciliation, fingerprint capture/revalidation, review/gate/test evidence, finalize, and plugin artifacts to those boundaries; port only the relevant design and tests from the old branch after adapting them to current main.
analysis.validation: The approach addresses the root problem by making the authority distinction a structural command contract instead of a per-call convention. Existing source already has FlowWorkspace and FlowSpecLocation in src/lib/flow-workspace.js, target binding/guarding in src/lib/flow-target-guard.js and src/lib/worktree-flow-binding.js, and repair fingerprint logic in src/flow/lib/repair-state-identity.js; the remaining draft questions focus on user-owned compatibility, migration, and verification boundaries rather than implementation mechanics.

knownFacts: must use issue #494 as a new current-main rebuild rather than reopening or mechanically importing old issue #491.
must treat base-side Flow artifacts and execution checkout state as separate authorities in worktree Flow.
must preserve the FlowTargetIdentityAuthority and recovery contracts introduced by issues #489-#493.
must not restore worktree-side spec copies as a second artifact authority.
must not relax target guard or step completion guard behavior.
must keep implementation within Node.js built-in modules and the repository's OOP class-based boundary style.
decisionPoints: must decide exact class names, constructor invariants, module placement, and method boundaries during spec writing.
must decide the detailed per-command authority matrix during spec writing from the named Flow surfaces and source audit.
resolvedByProjectRules: must not split this issue into multiple specs because project guardrails treat the user-defined issue as the scope boundary.
must use dedicated classes rather than object-literal type tags because AGENTS.md requires OOP for meaningful value constraints.
must not add external dependencies because project rules allow only Node.js built-in modules.
must define migration parity because this work moves or replaces existing Flow command behavior across public CLI surfaces.

must preserve retained public Flow CLI behavior for normal worktree and non-worktree flows while allowing fail-closed rejection of ambiguous raw-root misuse because alpha policy forbids legacy compatibility code and the issue is about enforcing authority boundaries.

must treat FlowTargetIdentityAuthority, target guard, dispatcher binding, recovery identity, and step completion guard behavior from issues #489-#493 as immutable compatibility behavior for this spec.

must require static audit evidence for raw-root artifact path construction because migration parity must inventory affected public surfaces and authority-sensitive path construction is the specific risk being refactored.
must allow spec authorship to choose final API names and module placement as long as class-based authority boundaries and verifiable authority guarantees are preserved.
deferredToSpec: must define the exact class names, constructor invariants, and module placement for artifact store, execution checkout, and command authority.
must inventory affected Flow command surfaces and map each retained public behavior to its new authority owner.
must define the file-map reconciliation boundary and fingerprint service contract at requirement granularity.
must map requirements to focused unit, E2E, static audit, and full regression verification.

must verify the entire named authority matrix across gate, review, set-step, test evidence, plugin artifact, finalize, dispatcher, and recovery; source audit may add surfaces but the draft does not require user-selected additional surfaces.
must use the old #491 branch only as design/test reference, with any manually adapted code pattern justified against current-main authority and recovery contracts.

in: must introduce or complete typed authority boundaries around FlowWorkspace for artifact store, execution checkout, and command authority.
must audit and migrate specs, task specs, file maps, issue logs, review/gate/test evidence, plugin artifacts, and finalize artifacts to base-side artifact authority.
must audit and migrate Git diff, HEAD, index, untracked source, implementation changes, and project tests to execution checkout authority.
must create migration-parity coverage for retained Flow command behavior across gate, review, set-step, test evidence, plugin artifact, finalize, dispatcher, and recovery surfaces.
must adapt authority-focused design and tests from the old branch only after reconciling them with current main.
out: must not reopen old issue #491 as the tracked work item.
must not bulk merge or cherry-pick old branch commits without current-main adaptation.
must not restore worktree-side spec copies as a fallback artifact authority.
must not weaken target guard, target identity binding, recovery, or step completion guards.
must not add external runtime dependencies.

impactOnExisting: must preserve user-facing Flow CLI behavior for normal worktree and non-worktree flows unless a behavior is explicitly documented as removed during this alpha refactor.
must affect Flow commands that read or write spec artifacts, issue logs, file maps, review/gate/test evidence, reports, finalize artifacts, and plugin artifacts.
must affect Flow commands that inspect or mutate implementation checkout state, including Git status/diff/fingerprint paths and project test execution.
must preserve existing target resolution, dispatcher binding, recovery, and side-effect-before-failure contracts introduced in issues #489-#493.

qa.question: 推奨: must treat this as a current-main authority-boundary rebuild, not as an old-branch merge. Is the goal to preserve the old #491 branch only as design/test reference while implementing against the current main authority and recovery model?
qa.answer: Yes. The spec must treat issue #494 as a current-main rebuild and may use the old #491 branch only as design/test reference, with any adapted material reconciled against the current target identity, dispatcher binding, recovery, and guard contracts.
qa.evidence: Issue framing in draft.analysis states #494 is new work on current main because the older #491 branch diverged from target identity and recovery changes from #489-#493; scopeVerification.out forbids bulk merge or cherry-pick of old branch commits without current-main adaptation.
qa.why: This follows the user-requested goal and avoids making stale branch state a second implementation authority.

qa.question: 推奨: must preserve retained public Flow CLI behavior through migration parity, but may fail closed for ambiguous raw-root misuse that was never a supported contract. Should the spec allow rejecting previously accepted raw string mix-ups at authority boundaries?
qa.answer: Yes. Retained public Flow CLI behavior must keep migration parity, but ambiguous raw-root mix-ups may be rejected fail-closed when they cross authority boundaries and were not a supported public contract.
qa.evidence: AGENTS.md alpha policy forbids legacy compatibility code; project migration-parity guardrail requires retained behavior mapping and explicit removal decisions; the issue goal is to replace raw repository/root-string authority-sensitive operations with explicit authority objects.
qa.why: Fail-closed rejection is the conservative outcome for an authority-boundary refactor and does not change the user-requested goal when limited to unsupported ambiguous misuse.

qa.question: 推奨: must cover the entire Flow command surface named in the issue, including gate, review, set-step, test evidence, plugin artifacts, finalize, dispatcher, and recovery. Are any additional Flow surfaces required for the authority matrix beyond these named areas?
qa.answer: No user-selected additional surfaces are required at draft-refine time. The spec must cover the named Flow surfaces and require a source audit to add any discovered authority-sensitive surfaces to the matrix.
qa.evidence: scopeVerification.in already names gate, review, set-step, test evidence, plugin artifact, finalize, dispatcher, and recovery; draft.decisionMap.deferredToSpec already requires inventorying affected Flow command surfaces.
qa.why: The existing issue and source-audit requirement define the mandatory breadth without needing an open-ended user decision.

qa.question: 推奨: must preserve the contract with FlowTargetIdentityAuthority from issue #493 and make repair-state identity use the same typed authority inputs for capture and revalidation. Should any target identity behavior be treated as immutable compatibility behavior for this spec?
qa.answer: Yes. FlowTargetIdentityAuthority, target guard matching, dispatcher binding, recovery identity, and step completion guard behavior introduced by issues #489-#493 must be treated as immutable compatibility behavior for this spec.
qa.evidence: draft.analysis identifies existing target binding/guarding in src/lib/flow-target-guard.js and src/lib/worktree-flow-binding.js plus repair fingerprint logic in src/flow/lib/repair-state-identity.js; knownFacts already require preserving FlowTargetIdentityAuthority and recovery contracts from #489-#493.
qa.why: The requested refactor is an authority-boundary rebuild on top of those contracts, not a redesign of target identity semantics.

qa.question: 推奨: must verify that updating only Flow artifacts does not change the implementation target fingerprint, while implementation source changes do. Is this fingerprint separation the primary acceptance signal for authority correctness?
qa.answer: Yes. Fingerprint separation is a primary acceptance signal, alongside command-surface migration parity and guard/recovery regression coverage.
qa.evidence: The issue goal separates base-side Flow artifact authority from execution checkout authority; draft.scopeVerification.in requires artifact writes to base-side authority and Git diff/HEAD/index/source/test operations to execution checkout authority.
qa.why: A fingerprint that ignores artifact-only updates but changes for implementation source updates directly demonstrates that the two authority domains are no longer mixed.

qa.question: 推奨: must not restore any worktree-side spec fallback or legacy per-command artifact-root inference path. Are there any legacy paths that should remain temporarily for operator diagnostics only, without participating in command authority?
qa.answer: No legacy artifact authority paths should remain as command participants. Diagnostic-only reporting may describe rejected legacy or ambiguous paths, but it must not read, write, or infer Flow artifact authority from them.
qa.evidence: knownFacts and scopeVerification.out both forbid restoring worktree-side spec copies as a second artifact authority; AGENTS.md alpha policy says not to keep deprecated paths or backward-compatibility code.
qa.why: Keeping legacy authority paths active would preserve the same ambiguity this spec is meant to remove.

qa.question: 推奨: must include focused authority tests plus node tests/run.js --scope unit and node tests/run.js --scope e2e as final verification. Should the draft require a static audit report for raw-root artifact path construction as a blocking acceptance item?
qa.answer: Yes. The spec should require a blocking static audit report for raw-root artifact path construction, in addition to focused authority tests and unit/e2e regression commands.
qa.evidence: The project migration-parity guardrail requires inventorying moved/replaced public behavior and mapping retained behavior to new owners; the draft goal identifies raw repository/root strings around artifact paths, execution paths, fingerprint inputs, and recovery evidence as the core problem.
qa.why: A static audit is necessary evidence that no authority-sensitive raw-root artifact construction remains outside the new authority boundaries.

qa.question: 推奨: should defer exact API names and constructor invariant details to the spec while requiring class-based boundaries. Is it acceptable for the spec to choose the final names and module placement if the authority guarantees remain verifiable?
qa.answer: Yes. Exact API names, constructor invariants, and module placement may be chosen during spec writing, provided the result uses class-based authority boundaries and keeps the authority guarantees verifiable.
qa.evidence: AGENTS.md requires OOP class-based representation for meaningful values; draft.decisionMap.deferredToSpec already assigns exact class names, constructor invariants, module placement, file-map boundary, and fingerprint service contract to spec writing.
qa.why: This is a spec-writing detail rather than a user-owned scope decision, as long as the required authority behavior remains testable.
